    <h2>Cole Rehbein</h2>
    <p class="terminal-subtitle-text">Crisis Counselor &amp; Clinical Psychology Researcher · Albuquerque, New Mexico</p>

    <p class="about-lead">Crisis counselor and clinical psychology researcher building reproducible tools for behavioral-health research, communication, and care.</p>

    <p>I work high-acuity crisis lines for Protocall Services (988 Suicide &amp; Crisis Lifeline network partner serving New Mexico) and am completing an M.S. in clinical psychology at New Mexico Highlands University, with a thesis on outdoor mindfulness-based behavioral activation for depression.</p>

    <h3>What I Do</h3>

    <p><strong>Crisis work.</strong> Crisis counselor with Protocall Services (988 Suicide &amp; Crisis Lifeline network partner serving New Mexico). High-acuity phone and chat triage and intervention, using ACT and behavioral activation. Friday–Monday nights.</p>

    <p><strong>Research.</strong> M.S. in clinical psychology at New Mexico Highlands University. Thesis: (outdoor) mindfulness-based behavioral activation for depression. Longitudinal design, psychometrics, psychological assessment, EEG. R for data work.</p>

    <p><strong>Building &amp; writing.</strong> This site — a Quarto/SCSS artifact, hand-set in monospace and deployed as static files — plus research tooling in R, Python, Quarto, Markdown, LaTeX, and Git, and science communication. Before clinical work: journalism as a city reporter, copyeditor, and culture writer.</p>

    <h3>Background</h3>

    <p><strong>Clinical training</strong> — Crisis intervention, ACT, behavioral activation. Graduate training in psychometrics, psychological assessment, and longitudinal research methods at New Mexico Highlands University.</p>

    <p><strong>Journalism</strong> — City reporting, copyediting, culture writing. Local politics, food, arts. Accuracy on a deadline.</p>

    <p><strong>St. John's College</strong> — B.A., philosophy (Great Books program). Close reading, Socratic dialogue, ancient Greek (reading).</p>

    <h3>Also true</h3>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Zazen:</strong> Sōtō Zen, personal practice — student, not teacher</li>
      <li><strong>Spinoza:</strong> ethics, philosophy of mind; the undergraduate focus that stuck</li>
      <li><strong>Systems thinking:</strong> class, power, institutional critique</li>
    </ul>

    <h3>Current Status</h3>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Thesis:</strong> data collection and analysis complete; manuscript in progress</li>
      <li><strong>Location:</strong> Albuquerque, New Mexico</li>
      <li><strong>Open to:</strong> behavioral-health research, mental-health technology, clinical data, and science communication roles</li>
    </ul>

    <h3>Contact</h3>

    <p><a href="mailto:cole@cole.press">cole@cole.press</a> — Email is best. I check it when I'm not on crisis lines.</p>
